headline: Why was Russell Brand sentenced to prison?
standfirst: British comedian and former Hollywood actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to ten and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault offences committed between 2004 and 2009.
keyPoints: Russell Brand received a total sentence of 10 years and six months in prison.
A jury found him guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
The crimes took place in London between 2004 and 2009 against four different women.
Judge Joel Bennathan described Brand as a sexual predator who abused his fame.

sections.heading: What are the details of the sentencing?
paragraphs: British comedian and former Hollywood actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to ten and a half years in a British prison following his conviction for rape and sexual assault. The sentencing took place at Southwark Crown Court in London, delivered by Judge Joel Bennathan after a jury found Brand guilty of offences against four women.

The legal proceedings followed a trial where prosecutors detailed attacks that occurred between 2004 and 2009. The jury convicted Brand on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, while clearing him of three other charges. The total prison term reflects nine years for the rape conviction, with additional consecutive and concurrent time added for the separate sexual assault charges.

sections.heading: How did the judge and prosecutors describe the crimes?
paragraphs: During the sentencing hearing, Judge Bennathan referred to Brand as a sexual predator who exploited his celebrity status and power to carry out the assaults and protect himself from accountability. The judge highlighted a staggering arrogance in Brand's behavior, noting that his public profile and surrounding entourage had enabled the abuse.

Crown prosecutors argued that Brand had caused severe psychological harm to his victims through degrading and humiliating treatment. Impact statements read aloud in court described the lasting trauma, anxiety, and profound disruptions the attacks caused in the survivors' personal and professional lives.

sections.heading: What was the defense argument?
paragraphs: Brand's defense team asked the court for mercy, arguing that his actions were isolated incidents and characterizing the rape as a short and momentary failure. His lawyers emphasized that Brand was now a changed man with a young family and asked the judge to consider leniency.

Despite these arguments, the prosecution successfully pushed for a heavy sentence within the category one penalty guidelines, pointing to the severity of the psychological damage inflicted and the breach of trust involved in the attacks.

sections.heading: What happens next?
paragraphs: With the sentencing concluded, Brand will begin serving his prison term, with eligibility for parole anticipated in several years subject to specific conditions. Police and prosecutors have publicly welcomed the verdict and used the moment to encourage other victims of sexual violence to come forward.

The high-profile case marks a dramatic downfall for a performer who achieved widespread fame in British television and radio before transitioning into Hollywood films and later building a prominent online political and cultural commentary presence.

highlight: Judge Bennathan referred to Brand as a sexual predator who exploited his celebrity status and power to carry out the assaults.
